reasoning: The core problem — that high linear-probe accuracy may reflect surface confounds rather than genuine concept signal — is a well-established and thoroughly addressed topic. Hewitt & Liang (2019) introduced exactly the control-task/selectivity methodology the proposal centers on (selectivity = task accuracy minus shuffled-label control accuracy), Belinkov (2021) surveys the full space of probing baselines/controls/shortcomings, and works like "Probing the Probing Paradigm" (2020) and "Probing Classifiers are Unreliable for Concept Removal and Detection" (NeurIPS 2022) directly cover the confound concern; diagNNose already provides a library implementing control tasks over extracted activations. The only genuine gap is engineering packaging: a single reusable, newcomer-oriented "probe sanity suite" that auto-trains the full battery (shuffled-label + bag-of-tokens + length/topic confounds) on TransformerLens activations and emits one diagnostic report, specifically targeting safety concepts like refusal — but the intellectual contribution (each control and metric) is fully published, so this is a minor packaging gap rather than a novel method.

evidence.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks (Hewitt & Liang, 2019)
evidence.summary: Foundational paper introducing control tasks (random/shuffled labels) and the selectivity metric (probe accuracy minus control-task accuracy) — exactly the central method the proposal proposes to package. Confirms the core diagnostic is already established.

evidence.title: Probing Classifiers: Promises, Shortcomings, and Advances (Belinkov, 2021)
evidence.summary: Survey synthesizing the probing-classifier validity problem, including the necessity of baselines and controls to distinguish genuine encoded information from probe memorization/confounds. Covers most of the conceptual contribution the proposal claims.

evidence.title: Probing the Probing Paradigm: Does Probing Accuracy Entail Task Relevance? (Ravichander et al., 2020)
evidence.summary: Directly investigates whether high probing accuracy reflects task-relevant signal or spurious cues, the exact question framed by the proposal's research question.

evidence.title: Probing Classifiers are Unreliable for Concept Removal and Detection (NeurIPS 2022)
evidence.summary: Shows probing classifiers latch onto spurious/confounding features rather than the target concept, reinforcing that the confound problem is well-characterized in published work.

evidence.title: diagNNose: A Library for Neural Activation Analysis
evidence.summary: An existing reusable library for extracting activations and training diagnostic classifiers with control-task functionality, partially overlapping the proposed reusable 'probe sanity suite' tooling contribution.

evidence.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes (John Hewitt, web tutorial)
evidence.summary: Author tutorial laying out control-task design and selectivity as standard practice, indicating the methodology is treated as established guidance rather than a novel contribution.
